Thanks again for the quick demo last week — the team found Redwood latency and cost numbers promising. We're running a 14‑day PoC and are two-thirds through our token allocation already. Would it be possible to grant an extra 150k eval credits to finish the remaining scenarios? We're running a batch of multi‑tenant prompts across a few datasets and the usage spiked unexpectedly.

I've attached a quick snapshot of the usage and the account map for context. Happy to hop on a call if you need more info.

Date: Thu, 28 Oct 2027 11:05:00 -0700

Hi Olivia — appreciate the context and the usage snapshot.

I can approve a one‑time 75k eval credit extension to cover the immediate spike so your engineers can finish the scenarios. Before I allocate more, can you confirm whether the workloads are all tied to a single org/account or if teams are spinning separate trial projects? We ask because we've seen some cases where multiple parallel trials inflate totals and we need to validate org topology.

Ben — tagging you since this looks like a larger PoC and could become a paid opportunity; if you want to approve a larger grant I'll need a quick thumbsup from revenue.

I'll schedule the 75k now once I hear back about the org mapping.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Nov 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: Request: additional eval credits for Aurelia PoC

Jordan / Neha — forwarding Olivia's request and Jordan's note. I pulled a quick inventory on Aurelia: three active trial org IDs from the same domain, two of which started within 48 hours of each other and are tied to closely overlapping IP ranges. I've attached a CSV with session_id, org_id, ip_subnet for the last 30 days.

Quick summary:
- org_a (primary) shows steady org‑level activity and a handful of engineers.
- org_b & org_c were created within 2 days of each other; usage pattern looks like parallel pilots likely run by the same team.
- There are multiple distinct payment/contact emails but same billing address and SSO domain.

This could be entirely legitimate (separate teams trialing in parallel), but it also matches patterns we've seen with coordinated trial expansion to maximize credits. Recommend security/compliance eyeball before we approve more than the one‑time 75k Jordan proposed.

Attachments: aurelia_org_usage_ip_30d.csv (csv)

Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: additional eval credits for Aurelia PoC

Thanks for the flag, Ben. I reviewed the org map + IP list and ran it through our abuse heuristics. Notable points:
- Three org_ids share the same OAuth client_id and identical SSO domain, but different billing contacts.
- Two orgs exhibit near‑identical prompt distributions and repeated short bursts at 03:00 UTC (likely automated testing).
- There are at least four machines (IP subnets) that appear in all three orgs' recent sessions.

Policy implications: this looks like coordinated parallel trials to extend free credits; it's on the boundary of allowed behavior. For a one‑time small extension (<=75k) we could proceed with close monitoring. Any larger grant should require:
  1) confirmation of separate POCs (email from distinct exec sponsor), or
  2) convert to paid pilot with a committed monthly minimum, or
  3) limit to a single org and transfer credits there.

I've attached a redacted SOC2 and our standard proforma for paid pilots in case sales pursues conversion.

Attachments: SOC2-redacted.pdf (pdf), pilot_proforma_v3.docx (docx)

Hi Olivia — thanks for the quick reply and for sharing the org map earlier. We've reviewed internally.

Short answer: we can provision the one‑time 75k eval credit extension I mentioned previously to let your engineers finish the scoped PoC in the primary org. We will not grant a larger cross‑org allocation at this time.

To proceed with the 75k:
- Please confirm which single org_id you want the credits applied to (reply with the exact org_id).
- If you want multiple teams to continue POCs, we can discuss converting the engagement to a paid pilot (see attached proforma Neha included).

Rationale: our monitoring flagged three trial orgs with overlapping identifiers and IP ranges; that pattern requires either consolidated org allocation or a paid conversion to avoid coordinated credit amplification. If you can provide distinct executive sponsors for each org and confirm separate budgets, we can revisit larger grants.

I've copied Marissa (revenue lead) so she can prioritize follow‑up if Aurelia indicates they're moving to a paid pilot.
